title: Config/Logging Anomaly Cleanup

findings: _cfg is correctly imported as 'from gpu_fuzzy_trader import config as _cfg' (run_pipeline.py:24) — attribute lookup works.
RB_GOVERNOR_ENABLED is a module-level constant defined unconditionally in config.py:1542 with type 'bool = True' — no import-time AttributeError risk.

New direct reference '_cfg.RB_GOVERNOR_ENABLED' is functionally equivalent to the existing 'bool(getattr(_cfg, "RB_GOVERNOR_ENABLED", False))' pattern used elsewhere in the same file (lines 534, 653, 746). Direct access is safe because the attribute is defined at module import; the defensive getattr pattern is only needed for truly optional config.

Early-return placement is correct: the SKIPPED branch is evaluated BEFORE results.get('phase3', {}) / results.get('phase4', {}), so it cannot read missing keys and is robust when RB Governor produces no phase3/phase4 results dict entries.
Docstring renumbering is consistent: legacy Phase 3+4 (5, 6), RB Governor (7), Phase 5 (8). Phase 5 renumbering from 7 to 8 is correct.
Comment is well-placed immediately above the field assignment at config.py:2107-2111.
Comment is informative and explains the WHY (small symbol sets 2-5, redundant with min_profitable_symbols gate, would be too aggressive).
Comment correctly references the gate that does the work (min_profitable_symbols), so a future reader can verify the rationale by inspecting the gate logic.
Value itself (True) is unchanged — purely a documentation change, no behavior delta.

No production code path executes differently. config.py change is comment-only. run_pipeline.py changes are: (a) docstring text only, (b) print branch that early-returns BEFORE any results.get lookup, leaving legacy Phase 3/4 summary code untouched when RB_GOVERNOR_ENABLED is False.
Phase 5 renumbering in docstring (7→8) is text-only and does not affect execution.
evaluator_v5.ipynb is NOT in the diff — confirmed by git diff --stat and explicit grep across .ipynb files. Acceptance criterion met.

C3 was marked optional in task-23.md ('only implement if it can be done cleanly without changing behavior for the no-remainder case'). Implementer correctly deferred. Acceptable — task scope is C1+C2, and no-remainder behavior must be preserved to avoid invalidating prior benchmark runs.
PYTEST_LOW_MEMORY=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_phase2_island_scheduler.py -x -q → 12 passed in 2.83s. No regressions.

minor_nits.description: Minor style inconsistency: existing RB Governor checks in run_pipeline.py use 'bool(getattr(_cfg, "RB_GOVERNOR_ENABLED", False))' (lines 534, 653, 746) while the new code uses direct '_cfg.RB_GOVERNOR_ENABLED'. Both are functionally equivalent here (attribute is always defined), but matching the existing defensive pattern would improve uniformity. Non-blocking.
minor_nits.recommendation: Optional: align with existing getattr pattern for stylistic consistency. Not required for approval.

summary: All acceptance criteria met. C1 docstring/summary updates are correct, properly placed, and gated on a real config flag. C2 comment is clear and explains the rationale. No behavior changes. evaluator_v5.ipynb untouched. 12/12 unit tests pass. C3 (optional budget-remainder fix) appropriately deferred per task spec. APPROVED.
